title: Delhi's Winter Pollution Curbs Begin: Vehicle Ban and 50% Work From Home
excerpt: From November 1 to January 31, non-Delhi vehicles below BS-VI are barred, offices must cap attendance at 50%, dust-generating construction is banned and parking charges have doubled.
body:
• Delhi's seasonal winter pollution framework is in force from November 1: petrol and diesel vehicles registered outside Delhi that do not meet BS-VI standards are barred from entering or plying in the capital until January 31.
  • Government and private offices must limit physical attendance to 50% until January 31, with the rest of the staff working from home; essential and emergency services are exempt.
  • Dust-generating demolition and outdoor civil construction are banned until January 31, except for essential public infrastructure projects, and parking charges at authorised sites are doubled until February 28.
  • More than 10 lakh vehicles registered in neighbouring NCR districts could be affected by the vehicle rule; enforcement uses ANPR cameras and an AI-enabled command centre, and vehicles without a valid pollution certificate will be denied fuel.

Delhi's winter pollution season now opens with a fixed set of restrictions, whether the day's air is bad or merely poor. The Delhi government's seasonal framework, notified on June 23, took effect on November 1 and runs in phases through January and February, alongside the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) — where the two overlap, the stricter GRAP provision applies, according to a Delhi government statement reported by Urban Acres.

The vehicle rule: who is barred

The widest measure covers vehicles registered outside Delhi. Petrol and diesel vehicles that do not meet BS-VI emission standards may not enter or ply in Delhi from November 1 to January 31 — a rule that could affect more than 10 lakh vehicles registered in neighbouring National Capital Region districts such as Noida, Gurugram and Ghaziabad. Exempt are CNG and electric vehicles, and emergency and government-duty vehicles including ambulances, fire tenders and police vehicles. Violating vehicles face automatic e-challans through number-plate recognition cameras and can be impounded by traffic police. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa told The Hindu that enforcement would initially focus on Delhi's borders.

Offices, construction and parking

Delhi government and private offices must cap physical attendance at 50% from November 1 to January 31, with remaining staff working from home and essential services exempt. Office hours are staggered to spread the commute: Delhi government offices work 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. and Municipal Corporation of Delhi offices 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. until February 28. Dust-generating demolition and outdoor civil construction are prohibited until January 31 except for essential public infrastructure. Parking charges at authorised facilities are doubled from November 1 to February 28, except at parking owned and managed by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation.

Enforcement and the fuel rule

Compliance is monitored by special enforcement teams through automatic number-plate recognition cameras and an AI-enabled Integrated Command and Control Centre, with the Transport Department, Delhi Traffic Police, the Delhi Pollution Control Committee and municipal agencies directed to enforce the measures, New Kerala reported. A separate year-round rule bars fuel stations from selling fuel to vehicles without a valid Pollution Under Control Certificate. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta appealed to citizens, vehicle owners, construction agencies and commercial establishments to follow the curbs.

How this sits with GRAP

The seasonal framework is a shift from relying mainly on pollution-triggered emergency measures. GRAP restrictions, announced by the Commission for Air Quality Management in stages as air quality worsens, still apply on top — the commission has separately announced a halt on construction and demolition across the NCR from November 5 to 20, and a complete construction and demolition ban, with specified exemptions, is scheduled from December 10 to January 20. The fixed measures, by contrast, stay in place for their full term even if the air temporarily improves.
